subject: Close-to-Live cadence, canary plan, and evaluation sprint — PioneerMed
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Donnelly <claire.d@pioneermed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Close-to-Live cadence, canary plan, and evaluation sprint — PioneerMed

Claire —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a concise close-to-live cadence that embeds the MAP deliverables, the evaluation sprint for the core flows, and the canary/migration guardrails. The goal here is to keep the first 4 weeks predictable (latency, error rate) while giving you deterministic rollback points.

High-level (attached: PioneerMed_MAP_v1.pdf):
- Week 0 (pre-cut): final acceptance of canary keystones and training roster due — target 3 business days after signature.
- Week 1 (canary): run 10% traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool with a dedicated canary model variant (quantized) for 72 hours. Evaluation sprint runs in parallel.
- Week 2 (scale test): 50% traffic with load runbooks and KV cache prewarm.
- Week 3 (ramp): 100% traffic and start rollback validation window.

Evaluation sprint scope (attached: canary-validation-checklist.xlsx):
- Acceptance prompts (10 canonical prompts) + 5 negative/regression prompts
- Latency SLO: median <= 120ms for 95th token window
- Quality SLO: no more than 2 regressions vs baseline on majority-vote evals
- Incident playbook: automatic fallback to hosted variant if error rate > 1.5% for 10m
Training and handoff:
- Two 90-minute sessions for product & ops (Week 0 and Week 2). Training cadence and slides attached (training-cadence-outline.docx).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the training attendee list and preferred dates (Week 0).
2) We lock the canary variant config and the 10 canonical prompts.
3) Sign-off on the MAP PDF — I can update and re-upload.

Ben and Marcus — FYI on the timeline and the quick validation checklist. Marcus will own the canary gates; Ben will take the training coordination.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk through the checklist.

Best,

Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
E: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: PioneerMed_MAP_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); canary-validation-checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB); training-cadence-outline.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

From: Claire Donnelly <claire.d@pioneermed.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Prasad <rajesh.p@pioneermed.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:28:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Close-to-Live cadence, canary plan, and evaluation sprint — PioneerMed

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the attachments. This looks good; a few clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) Canary traffic: we want the 10% to include only a subset of our beta customers (region: east coast). That works operationally?
2) Training attendees: I can confirm two engineers (Rajesh + Maya) and one product manager (Claire). Week 0 preferred dates: June 2 or June 3.
3) Baseline evaluation: do you have an example baseline dataset format you prefer?

Also, two asks from security: we need the exact KV cache retention window called out in the MAP (we currently have a 7-day retention policy internally).

Can you get back to us on the above by EOD Tuesday so we can align procurement sign-off?

Appreciate it —

Claire
Director, Product Operations
PioneerMed
E: claire.d@pioneermed.com | T: +1 (212) 555-0192

Claire —

Thanks — answers inline below and some asks for our side so we can keep procurement moving:

1) Canary traffic regional scope: yes — we can scope the 10% to East Coast beta IDs. We'll tag traffic by region at the routing layer and confirm sampling before cut. Marcus will coordinate a short smoke pass.

2) Training: Jun 2 at 10:00am PT works for us. Ben, can you confirm the invite and attach the slides?

3) Baseline dataset: see Drive link (MAP_v1 -> folder "evaluation-sprint"). Preferred format is CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_intent, acceptance_notes. We'll add a template to the folder by EOD.

Security / KV retention: Redwood's default KV cache retention for canary variants is 48 hours. That can be configured to 7 days if you need persistent warm state across long windows — note there is a cost delta and some privacy considerations. If PioneerMed requires 7-day retention we will surface that for procurement as a special config.

Procurement note: we will need a signed SOW for the Dedicated canary pool and the training sessions. If you can route this to your procurement by Tue EOD we can keep the June 2 training.

Ben / Marcus — can you confirm: 1) Marcus to own the canary smoke pass (tagging plan + pre-cut verification). 2) Ben to send training invites & slides. Also adding Rajesh on the evaluation template so he can drop the canonical prompts.

Thanks —

Aisha
